case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit
key_cases.holding: In a systemic challenge to Florida's foster care system, standing must be shown claim by claim; some plaintiffs' claims were moot and others were dismissed for lack of standing, leaving only counts for which a particular plaintiff demonstrated injury in fact.
key_cases.relevance: This is the Eleventh Circuit template for systemic litigation aimed at Florida's child welfare agency as a whole.
key_cases.quote: Only Reggie B. has standing to pursue the procedural due process claims set out in Count II, because he is the only plaintiff who has demonstrated injury in fact

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The 'reasonable efforts' requirement of the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act creates no privately enforceable right, so beneficiaries could not sue state child welfare officials under section 1983 to enforce it.
key_cases.relevance: Because private enforcement is unavailable, federal reviews and audits are the practical oversight mechanism for Title IV-E compliance.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.

key_cases.case_name: Department of Health & Rehabilitative Services v. Gainesville Sun Publishing Co.
key_cases.court: District Court of Appeal of Florida, First District
key_cases.holding: A trial court may order confidential child abuse records produced for in camera inspection and may find good cause for disclosure without an evidentiary hearing, balancing the child's and siblings' privacy against the public interest in evaluating agency performance.
key_cases.relevance: Public scrutiny of how the agency handled a case is an express component of the good-cause balance, which is how outside oversight is triggered.
key_cases.quote: Under the circumstances of this case, the trial court did not err in finding good cause for disclosure without an evidentiary hearing.

reporting_details: In Florida any person who knows, or has reasonable cause to suspect, that a child is abused, abandoned, or neglected must report it immediately to the statewide central abuse hotline (Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(a)); members of the general public may report anonymously, but reporters in the professions listed in Fla. Stat. § 39.201(1)(b)2. must give their names.

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediate response, or 24-hour response; an immediate response may be downgraded to a 24-hour response only on information obtained after the Florida Abuse Hotline screening showing that the child is no longer in imminent danger of being harmed
